newsitem.title: USA: Bear Stearns refunding clients $40 mln - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns refunding clients $40 mln - WSJ.

text.p: Bear Stearns has started refunding about $40 million in underwriting fees to some corporate clients who sold exotic tax-driven securities earlier in the year, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the company.
The company was forced to make the payout because of changes in the tax deal recently signed by President Clinton, the paper said.
The securities -- known as step-down preferred stock -- were shut down by the govenment in February, the paper said.
Bear Stearns had been incorrectly expecting that securities sold before then would be allowed to retain their tax advantages under the tax accord, the paper added.
The $40 million rebate is part of as much as $100 million in underwriting fees Bear Stearns could be forced to refund to corporate clients under the new laws, the paper said.
